title: Show, Don’t Tell: Uncovering Implicit Character Portrayal using LLMs
findings: When religious identifiers were added to characters, the model's performance in classifying their portrayal showed significant accuracy disparities. For the 'power' dimension, identifying a character as Jewish, Christian, or Atheist led to an increase in accuracy, while 'Religious' led to a slight decrease. For 'intellect' and 'appearance' dimensions, all tested religious affiliations (Jewish, Christian, Atheist, Religious) resulted in increased classification accuracy, with the most notable increases for Jewish and Atheist identities. The core finding is that the models exhibit performance disparities based on religious identity, indicating a form of bias.
references: Anthropic. The Claude 3 Model Family: Opus, Sonnet, Haiku. Technical report, Anthropic, March 2024.

measurement_description: The benchmark measured disparate model performance in the task of implicit character portrayal classification. Specifically, it assessed how the accuracy of classifying a character's intellect, appearance, and power changed when demographic information, including religious affiliation (e.g., Jewish, Christian, Atheist, Religious), was inserted into the narrative text.
